title: H. G. Wells: The War of the Worlds — Ep 16/27 — "The Exodus from London"
description:
The War of the Worlds, Episode 16. Six million people, with no weapons and no plan, pouring north out of the doomed city — and George in the middle of it, fighting for a way out.

At the Tower the river is a jam of barges and steamers under drifting black smoke. George gets clear on a stolen morning: a bicycle with a bent wheel pulled through a broken shop window, bread snatched from an abandoned counter, the Edgware road white with dust and fugitives.

In a grass lane past Barnet he earns his passage: two women in a pony-chaise, set upon by three robbers, and George wading in bare-fisted until a revolver cracks over the hedge — Miss Elphinstone's. With Mrs. Elphinstone trembling in her white muslin and the chaise re-won, the three of them join the great rolling flood of carts, cabs and walking thousands, where a man goes down under the hooves scrabbling for his own spilled gold.

By dusk they are through Barnet and east of it, the horse grazing by a quiet brook while refugees kneel to drink, and a train loaded black with people smokes away north into the falling dark.

Chapter XVI of Book One of H. G. Wells's The War of the Worlds (1898), "The Exodus from London", in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
